newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: 3Com sees more price cuts in products.
newsitem.headline: 3Com sees more price cuts in products.

text.p: U.S. networking company 3Com Corp is likely to continue cutting prices of its products by 15-20 percent annually, chairman and chief executive officer Eric Benhamou said on Thursday.
The company's ongoing merger with U.S. Robotics, expected to be completed in summer, should result in few job losses, he told Reuters.
"I expect the price reductions will continue. In the past we've seen price cuts of about 15-20 percent per year and this is likely to continue," Benhamou said.
He said 3Com saw price cuts of 20-40 percent for its various networking products in February which partially impacted the company's fiscal third quarter earnings.
The impact of the cuts will spill over into the fourth quarter, he said.
For the third quarter ended February 28, 1997, 3Com reported a net profit of US$87.6 million on sales of US$786.8 million.
Benhamou said 3Com had nudged its gross margins higher to 53-55 percent from 52-54 percent previously. He said the margins would be maintained through cost management despite the price cuts.
On whether there would be redundancies from its merger with consumer modem giant U.S. Robotics, Benhamou said:

"The two companies have almost no overlaps. Obviously there will be a few jobs that will be redundant. People will have the opportunities to move into other jobs. I expect there would be some but not in large amounts."
3Com is in the process of merging with U.S. Robotics in a stock deal valued at US$7.3 billion.
